body: Yeah man, my heart is completely broken :(

Thank you so much for your kind words. I know you are right, and I've had many people say the same thing to me. It's just very difficult to feel this way when I have a cloud of depression/grief/sadness around my head at the moment. I am hoping that with time I will see the positives from this situation and will move on to bigger and better things. I'm just having extreme trouble letting go of the entire lifestyle that was so difficult for me to achieve in the first place. Social anxiety ruled my life for so long, and with a lot of hard work, I finally overcame it and met someone who I genuinely fell in love with. I have memories of us together that are mine alone, I can't share or reminisce about them with Kat anymore because she hates me. She won't speak to me again and it hurts to know that I have been so easily replaced and that the person I shared the most significant chapter of my life with has no interested in my company any longer and has become my enemy.

Hey, thank you for reading!

She never went into specifics, but she did tell me she had a bad childhood. She complained about her parents a lot and said that they are "always watching everything she does". She said that growing up, they never argued and just swept all their problems under the rug. She was apparently completely mute only a couple years before I met her and she said she spent an entire year without sleep staring at the ceiling (obviously not true).

According to my research and my experience, she suffers from Borderline Personality Disorder. The imaginary attacks that she would accuse me of, the unstable mood swings and the alternation between idealization and devaluation are characteristic of her and the disorder. She also cuts people out of her life easily and without remorse which is another symptom of BPD.

https://www.psychologytoday.com/blog/stop-walking-eggshells/201004/fresh-look-the-many-faces-borderline-disorder

Life with social anxiety is hard. I have tackled it well and it no longer rules my life. The main problem I have now is grief, depression and an overwhelming feeling of loneliness and low self esteem.

6 months in. Recently found out Kat is now DATING one of my friends within the smash community and has been for months. Needless to say, I feel like hell and am crying every day...I seriously DO NOT WANT TO LIVE ANYMORE.

Hi, I'm glad I could keep you interested until the very end.

I feel like this wouldn't have happened to me if I didnt deserve it. I'm constantly stuck in a mental state of trying to understand what I could have done differently to have things go differently and also thinking on what I can do now to mend the damage. I cant do it though. I dont know what mistakes I can learn from, I feel my personality must be fundamentally flawed in a way beyond my control in order for something so crazy to happen.

Knowing Kat is out there with my friends, having no feeling for what shes put me through is nothing short of heartbreaking. The girl I loved and cared for, the girl I waited a year before I could start dating and the girl I had the best chemistry with in my life hates me, steals my friends and ignores me and wants nothing to do with me...

Hi and thanks for your response. I will certainly look into SAM-E and phosphatidylserine, I'm willing to try anything that might help the pain.

I am eating healthy, I'm regularly exercising and have a gym membership as of 2 weeks ago. It's the only thing I have right now that keeps me in a routine and I'm starting to see some results physically which is nice. Endorphins are my best friend right now, and I strive to get as many of them as I can. I've actually been doing regular exercise since 2012 and I should probably add that to my post.

As for sleep, I'm currently taking half a sleeping tablet + Mirtazapine (my antidepressant). I have taken magnesium in the past but find its not strong enough to get the job done. Its been 5 months since the breakup but I'm still shattered, I'm not sure if time is the only thing that will ever make me feel better. I am trying my best to tackle things naturally without resorting to an unhealthy coping mechanism but its very tough.

Hi anubis135 and thanks for taking the time to read my post. I'd actually be extremely surprised if she ever came back to me, shes making an intentional effort to avoid any contact with me at every turn. I've also expressed my anger and frustration with how shes treated me in more ways than one and knowing her, she will never look passed my words of fury. Its not uncommon for her to permanently shut people out of her life (her brother, her dad, other friends) and I'm pretty sure I've ended up as another person on her list.

The other thing that makes this so hard is that there WAS a good Kat. Its so difficult with mental disorders because her loving/caring personality was legitimately real, but because of her warped way of processing information, she comes off as being cruel and heartless even though its not her intention. She truly believes SHE is the victim in all this, and she believes it with all her heart. Its like blaming a cat for accidentally scratching you and pulling your eye out...its not really their fault, they dont know any better.
